title: Enrolling a Private Service Edge
aliases: oauth2 user code private service edge
private service edge deleted by mistake

prose.text: Enrolling a Private Service Edge is the step that gives an added instance its identity in a group.

prose.label: Terraform side.
prose.text: {{tf-two-methods}} {{tf-provisioning-key}} [[zpa.terraform.group-enrollment:resolver-lookup-by-name]] Failure to verify user codes after the group is written is a provider behavior: [[zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity:user-code-verification-after-write]]. Association types for provisioning keys: [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects:provisioning-key-all-associations-fixed-list]]. OAuth2 licensing beyond the version is open {{gap:oauth2-prerequisites}}. The module's OAuth2 default and provider minimum are in [[zpa.private-service-edges.reference-modules]].

enrollment-tokens-preferred.statement: Configuring a Private Service Edge involves adding it in the Admin Console, which includes applying enrollment tokens (preferred) or obtaining a Private Service Edge provisioning key, and then deploying it on a supported platform.

quotes: Configuring Private Service Edges involves two main tasks:
Adding Private Service Edges using the Zscaler Admin Console, which includes applying enrollment tokens (preferred) or obtaining a Private Service Edge provisioning key.
Deploying Private Service Edges on the supported platform of your choice.

oauth-name-format.statement: OAuth-enabled Private Service Edges are added with a name in the format GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp.

quotes: OAuth-enabled Private Service Edges are added with a name format of GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp.

listed-only-when-deployed.statement: The Private Service Edges page lists deployed instances; instances that were added but not deployed are not listed.

quotes: View a list of all deployed Private Service Edges.
but have not deployed are not listed.

enrollment-cert-shown.statement: A Private Service Edge shows the enrollment certificate used to authenticate it during enrollment.

quotes: The certificate used to authenticate Private Service Edges during the enrollment process.

tf-two-methods.statement: The Terraform Service Edge group resource supports two onboarding methods: OAuth2 user codes, recommended for new deployments, and a provisioning key, described as legacy and still supported.

quotes: ZPA Private Service Edges can be onboarded into ZPA in two ways. This resource supports both:
OAuth2 user codes
recommended for new deployments
legacy / still supported
Provisioning key

tf-provisioning-key.statement: For the provisioning-key method, a zpa_provisioning_key is created after the group that references the group's ID and the SERVICE_EDGE_GRP association type; the key is injected into the Private Service Edge VM at deployment.

quotes: ZPA Private Service Edges can be onboarded into ZPA in two ways. This resource supports both:
Create the Service Edge Group, then create a `zpa_provisioning_key` that references the group's ID.
association_type   = "SERVICE_EDGE_GRP"
The provisioning key is then injected into the Service Edge VM at deployment time.
evidence.after: ## Example Usage - Enrolling Service Edges Via Provisioning Key (Explicit Enrollment Certificate)

deleted-pse-unrecoverable.statement: A Private Service Edge deleted from the console by accident is immediately refused by Private Access and cannot be recovered; the instance must be cleaned on the host (service stopped, /opt/zscaler/var/* removed, service restarted) and the configure-and-deploy process restarted.

quotes: You might see this error if a Private Service Edge was deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console accidently.
Private Access immediately recognizes that it should not communicate with the Private Service Edge, and it breaks the active connection. There is no way to recover the Private Service Edge.
sudo systemctl stop zpa-service-edge
rm -rf /opt/zscaler/var/*
Restart the services.
Restart the process for configuring a Private Service Edge and deploying on a platform.

enrollment-steps.statement: A Private Service Edge first generates a local private key encrypted with a hardware fingerprint, then enrolls: it generates a Certificate Signing Request, authenticates it with the provisioning key from the Admin Console, receives a signed TLS client certificate from the Private Access cloud, and the certificate is pinned to its hardware fingerprint. Once enrolled it is paired with a single customer account and cannot be enrolled again.

quotes: the Private Service Edge must first generate the local private key, which it encrypts using a hardware fingerprint.
The Private Service Edge uses the local private key to generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR).
It uses the provisioning key to authenticate the CSR to the Private Access cloud. This is the provisioning key that you generated in the Zscaler Admin Console
It receives a signed TLS client certificate from the Private Access cloud.
The signed TLS client certificate is pinned to the Private Service Edge's hardware fingerprint.
it is paired with a single customer account, and it cannot be enrolled again.

pse-clone-rule.statement: Private Service Edges running in VM environments should never be cloned, because the keys will no longer match the virtual hardware fingerprints.

quotes: Private Service Edges that are running in virtual machine (VM) environments should never be cloned, because the keys will no longer match the virtual hardware fingerprints.

same-provisioning-key-scales.statement: Additional Private Service Edges can be deployed at any time with the same provisioning key to join the existing group.

quotes: You can deploy additional Private Service Edges at any time, using the same provisioning key to add them to the existing Private Service Edge group

oauth-min-version.statement: OAuth 2.0 enrollment requires Manager software and Private Service Edge version 25.48.4 or later, and an enrollment token from a hyperscaler marketplace, virtual image or RPM installer provided by Zscaler (or a provisioning key); the OAuth server supports IPv4 only.

quotes: For OAuth 2.0 enrollment, Manager software and Private Service Edge version 25.48.4 or later

An OAuth 2.0 enrollment token obtained from a hyperscaler marketplace, virtual image, or RPM installer provided by Zscaler, or a Private Service Edge provisioning key obtained from the Zscaler Admin Console
The OAuth server only supports IPv4-based communication.

oauth2-prerequisites.title: Licensing and tenant prerequisites for OAuth2 enrollment
oauth2-prerequisites.detail: The version prerequisite is stated, but whether OAuth2 enrollment needs a license or tenant-side enablement is not. Resolve with tenant confirmation or Zscaler support.

pse-provisioning-key-terraform.title: Whether Private Service Edge provisioning keys can be managed through Terraform
pse-provisioning-key-terraform.resolution: Yes: a zpa_provisioning_key with the SERVICE_EDGE_GRP association type, referencing the group (claim tf-provisioning-key).
